title: He rose slowly and, recalling the rapture of his sleep, sighed at its joy
html_source:
At the end of this chapter Stephen has an epiphany – he realizes that he wants to become an artist! Stephen tends to reach emotional highs and lows at the end of each chapter. James Joyce was very fond of his characters experiencing epiphanies. In fact, there is a specific name for it – the Joycean Epiphany. In general, an epiphany is an experience of sudden realization. In a Joycean Epiphany, the realization is usually blown out of proportion or not very logical. Stephen does tend to be pretty dramatic at times.
